In the future, O King of kings, the eighteen Purāṇas, the Nārasiṃha-carita, as well as the various Dharma-śāstras, the Śiva-dharmas from the Mahābhārata, the five Vedas including the Kaṭha, and the Śiva-dharma spoken by Manu—O Lord of the Earth, the wise declare that the name of these is "Japa. Having first recited the Praṇava (Oṃ), one should read the hymn and the Saṃhitā; at the end, one should offer the Praṇava.

The Primordial Being (Ādipurusha) said: It should indeed be understood that this [text] must be recited everywhere; otherwise, it would be fruitless. One who is pure and focused on nothing else should recite with a concentrated mind.

Recitation of the hymn (stotra) must not be performed by one whose mind is incapable or distracted. Having placed the book upon its support, the wise man should read it aloud. For merely holding it in the hand yields little fruit. Whether it was written by oneself or written by a skilled scribe—[this applies to] the Brāhma...

Even that which has been written down would become fruitless. A wise person should perform the *ṛṣi*-vidyā and other nyāsas; however, if the stotra is not seen in the recitation, one should perform the *praṇava-nyāsa* for the son. Having determined the number for the intended recitation of the stotra, the intelligent one should recite it. Upon reaching the end of a chapter (*adhyāya*), he should pause, but never in the middle. If a pause occurs in the middle, he should recite the beginning of the chapter again. In this regard, all worshippers of Caṇḍī...

Having performed the *ṛṣi-ṣaḍaṅga* (the assignment of the seer and the six limbs) for Nārāyaṇa, and having recited its *guhya*, *argala*, and *kīlaka* mantras once; then, having performed the *ṛṣi-ṣaṣṭha-aṅga* for Navāṇa, and having meditated upon it, one should recite the *amala* mantra one hundred and eight times. Having offered it with the mantra beginning with "guhye," one should then recite the *mālā-mantra* starting from "Sāvarṇiḥ sūryaḥ" up to the end of the *Sāvarṇi-manu* section—having fully understood the *argha-pada* and the *ucādi* (the sequence of syllables)—and then, as before, recite it one hundred and eight times. Then... [the text continues].

In this manner, there should be a single recitation (*sakṛjjapa*) of the *Śatacaṇḍī* and other such [mantras], as well as the *Rahasya* and others. Likewise, the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) should each perform the recitation daily: one hundred times on the first day, two hundred on the second, three hundred on the third, and four hundred on the fourth. Regarding the diet of the priests and the performer of the rite, they should subsist daily on milk alone; however, if unable to do so, they may consume sacrificial food (*haviṣyānna*). Alternatively, one should feed one hundred or one thousand Brahmins every day. This is the rule for recitation (*japavidhi*). Now follows the rule for the fire-oblation (*homavidhi*).

Regarding this, some say that for the *Navacaṇḍī* rite, the fire-oblation (*homa*) is performed on the eighth day; for the *Śatacaṇḍī*, on the fifth day; and for the *Sahasracaṇḍī*, on the eleventh day. Others assert that for the *Navarātra*, the oblation is performed on the ninth day. This is unexamined and not at all pleasing. Furthermore, they claim that on the ninth day there is the dismissal (*visarjana*) of the Goddess’s water-pot (*kalaśa*) or the lamp; that too is a manifestation of ignorance. Regarding the specific methods of worship beginning from the first lunar day (*pratipad*), it is stated in the *Bhaviṣya Purāṇa* concerning the materials for the grooming of the hair: "One should offer... [and so forth].

Beginning with the first day of the lunar fortnight, one should observe fasting; then on the eighth day, worship according to one's capacity, as well as fasting and fire-offerings (*homa*). On the ninth day, Bhadrakālī—who destroyed the sacrifice of Dakṣa by means of incense and lamps—manifested in her most terrible form along with millions of *yoginīs*. Therefore, she should be worshipped with offerings on that day by men who have fasted, using incense, lamps, garments, garlands, and ointments. This refers specifically to the worship of the ninth day alone.

One who has received initiation (*abhiṣeka*) should worship Varada, Aśuka, and the Aśvins; therefore, the wise should perform the complete worship of Caṇḍikā on that very [eighth day] and on the ninth.

Regarding the five-fold division beginning with the first lunar day (*pratipad*), just as the time for sacrifice is established on the first day of the festival, so too is it well-known that the commencement of the fire-oblation (*homa*) is on the eighth, the offering of the sacrificial oblation (*bali*) on the ninth, and the ritual dismissal (*visarjana*) on the tenth. Now, concerning the *homa*: having combined what is prescribed in one's own *Gṛhya-sūtra* with what is found in the *Āgama*, and having performed that which is prescribed in the *Gṛhya-sūtra*, one should follow the *Āgama*.
One should perform that which has been prescribed; therein lies the determination. In the *Rudrayāmala*:

"For those performing Vedic rites, one should not practice the Tāntrika; for the Tāntrika, one should not perform Vedic rites in any way. Thus, some maintain that because the Tāntrika is Vedic, it supersedes the other. Now, as for the question of whether it belongs to one's own Śākhā or otherwise, [the *Bhāgavata* states]: "One should worship the Lord with Vedic [mantras], and Keśava with that which is declared therein [in the Tāntra]. Thus, there is both the Vedic and the Tāntrika.

Because it was previously enjoined in this manner, the Vedic [rite] is concise, whereas the Tantric one involves meditation (*dhyāna*) and so forth, worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*) with its enclosures (*sāvaraṇa*), and a greater abundance of fruit. As it is stated in the *Sphāṭa*:

"If it is argued that after the worship of the enclosures and so forth has been described previously, the Tantric rite alone should be performed, [we reply]: according to the maxim of the 'increasing vessel' (*vardhamānaparibhāṣā*), you ought not to abandon what is based on your own branch (*śākhā*) to perform what is based on another branch; for that would be the act of one who is dull-witted. Garga also says: [...]* *Note: The ellipsis indicates the missing portion of the source text.*
If a Brahmin, out of delusion, performs Vedic rites with disregard for the Smārta and Itihāsa traditions, he is not joined with merit. Vedic action is primary;
one who is devoted to the subsequent qualities [of the secondary rites] while the Vedic action remains subordinate falls into a downward state because of the obstruction caused by that fault.

If it is asked, "In that case, what is the status of the performance of Tantric practices such as the *Saptaśatī*? [the answer is found] in the *Kulārṇava*: "One should perform the Vedic and the Mantric [rites]; within the Tantric, the Vedic..."

"Otherwise, all action that is mixed with both [Vedic and Tantric] would become fruitless. Having stated this, some [claim] that Vedic bathing and so forth are sublated; others say they are not falsely sublated. The meaning is that the Vedic [rite] alone makes the Tantric one complete in its qualities (sāṅga), while the Tantric [rite] does not make the Vedic one complete in its qualities. Otherwise, due to a lapse in conduct, there would be the consequence of unfitness. For this very reason, it was stated in the *Pūjā-paṭala*: "Having performed..."

"One should first perform the Vedic *sandhyā* and then perform that [Tantric] *sandhyā*. Therefore, although there is unity in the performer, time, and deity between the Vedic and Tantric *sandhyās*, experts of the tradition (*sāṃpradāyavid*) maintain that they remain distinct ritual acts (*bhinnapadārtha*) because their constituent elements differ. Now, the procedure (*prayoga*): Having specified the place and time, for the sake of the fruit [of the rite], one should perform the recitation (*japa*) of either the *Navacaṇḍī*, *Saptacaṇḍī*, or *Sahasracaṇḍī* through the mediation of a Brāhmaṇa.

"I shall perform the *homa* with citron, sugarcane, rhinoceros horn, nutmeg, mango fruit, honey, and sesame seeds as prescribed—or with whatever materials are available—and I shall perform the purification of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), the installation of the fire, and so forth. Having thus made this formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*), one should then prepare the altar (*sthaṇḍila*) by smearing it and so on, according to the secret [tradition], ending with the rite for the removal of defects (*arśānta*).

This should be done likewise for a raised mound (*kuṭa*). Then, having gazed at it with the root mantra, sprinkled it, and struck it with a fruit, one should repeat "Hum" while brandishing the hand and "Phaṭ" while clapping.

Having performed the *tikhanana* (piercing with the trident), one should extract [the wood] gently with *phaṭ*. Then, filling it with *namaḥ*, leveling it with *phaṭ*, sprinkling it with *huṃ*, and striking it with the *astra-mantra*;

then applying ointment with *kankābhyo namaḥ*; making it into a thread according to the procedure stated in the root-text with the middle [finger] and *svaralāya*; worshipping it with *namaḥ*; making it adamantine (*vajrīkaraṇa*) with *phaṭ*; purifying it with *kuśa* grass with *namaḥ*; visualizing the crossroads with *vauṣaṭ*; and splitting the beads with *namaḥ*—having thus performed the eighteen purificatory rites (*saṃskāra*).

Alternatively, having performed the four purificatory rites beginning with sprinkling water and ending with the inspection (*avīkṣaṇa*), one should draw three lines from south to north with the root of *kuśa* grass using the mantra "Hṛdayāyanamaḥ," dedicated to the deity Viṣṇu-Rudra; then, having drawn three lines from west to east with the root of *kuśa* grass, dedicated to the deities Brahmā, Yama, and Candra, one should fashion a dot (*bindu*) there at the navel, and outside of that, a *yantra* consisting of a triangle, a circle, a six-pointed star, another circle, and a six-pointed star provided with four gates.

Then, having written [the mantra] and likewise meditated upon it, one should perform the rites up to the meditation on the fires (agnidhyāna), beginning with "juṣṭo dṛṣūṇā" and so forth. Then, having determined the five locations for the sacred fires—namely, the Āvasathyāgni in the middle, the Gārhapatya in the east, the Āhavanīya in the west, the Anvāhārya in the north, and the Gārhapatya in the south—one should sprinkle them with water using kuśa grass while reciting the mantra "Astrāya phaṭ. Then, having worshipped the Yoga-pīṭha with the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ sarvaśaktikamalāsanāya," [one should proceed].

There, having visualized Vāgīśvarī—who has bathed after her period, resembles a blue lotus, and is joined with Vāmeśvarī—one should, in that very womb which is the place of the assembly (*sabhya-sthāna*), bring forth the fire born from the sun, the lord of the seed of Śiva, and so on, within the house produced by the *Śrīpaga* syllable. Having brought it with the vessel of fire, one should discard the portion belonging to the flesh-eaters (*kravyādāṃśa*) in its center, establish it with the *praṇava*, join it with wood and other materials, and sprinkle it with the root mantra while reciting "phaṭ. Thus [ends the section].

Having sprinkled [the vessel] with *phaṭ*, having joined the consciousness with *oṃ raṃ*, having rendered it nectar-like by means of the *dhenumudrā* with *vam*, having protected it with *phaṭ*, and having veiled it with *huṃ*, one should worship three times with sandalwood paste (*gandha*), flowers, and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) preceded by the *praṇava* (oṃ) toward the east and other directions. Then, kneeling upon the ground, having visualized the fire facing oneself, and having offered the water for sipping (*ācamana*) to the deity and the divine attendants, [one recites]: *oṃ citvaṃ gala hana (2) daha (2) daha (2) paca (2)*.

Having kindled the fire with the mantra *sarvajñājñāpayasvāhā* using *kuśa* grass, one should worship the blazing fire with the verse: "I salute Agni, the consumer of oblations, who is the Jātavedas; he is golden-hued, established in the fire, and possesses faces on all sides. Standing there with palms joined in reverence (*añjali*), having performed the ritual salutation (*upasthāna*) and sipped water (*upaspṛśya*), one should perform the *sāttvika* rite by placing [the mantras] upon one's own body at the locations of the *liṅga* and other sites: In the *liṅga*: *tryūṃ hiraṇyāya inguhye śū gaganāyaiḥ* (at the secret place). At the head: *śi*. ... [The text continues with further placements]. (Note: The provided fragment ends mid-sentence regarding the placement of mantras on specific parts of the body.)

*Rasiṃ* to *Cūraktā* on the face; *Vyūṃ* to *Kṛṣṭyā* on the nose; *Lyūṃ* to *Suprabhā* on the two eyes; *Śiraṃ* to *Siṃśūṃbhaṃdra* and *Lohitā* on the head; as before, *Vurūpā* to [the forehead]; *Śrūṃ* to *Atiraktā* on all limbs. Thus having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) on the tongue, for rites involving desire (*kāmyakarman*), [one places]: *Tyūṃ* to *Padmarāgā* on the linga; *Ṣryūṃ* to *Suvarṇā* on the secret place; *Śyūṃ* to *Bhadralohitā* on the head; *Chūṃ* to *Lohitā* on the mouth; *Tyūṃ* to *Śvetā* on the nose.

In the act of killing (*yainakraya*): *yaṃ* on the chest for Pūdhūminī; on all limbs for Śrūkaṃrālikā; in the case of cruel rites (*krūrakarman*), *tuṃ* on the genitals for Viśvamūrti; on the secret place (*guhya*) for Śrūsphuliṅginī; on the head for Śryūdhūmravarṇā; on the face for Chūṃ Manojavā; on the nose for Lyūṃ Lohitā;
on the two eyes for Prūṃ Karālākhyā; and on all limbs for Śrūṃ Kālātā. Thus, having performed that rite, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) upon the tongue and one's own body.

Then, one should perform the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*): *sahasrārciṣe hṛdayāya svāhā*; *svasti pūrṇāya śirase svāhā*; *uttiṣṭha puruṣāya śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*; *dhūmravyāpine kavacāya huṃ*; *sasaptajihvāya netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*; *dhanurdharāya astrāya phaṭ*. Having thus performed the six-limbed assignment, one should then place [the mantras]: "Salutation to Agni Jātavedas" on the head; "To Agni Saptajihva" on the left shoulder; and on the left side.

"Obeisance to Agni Havyavāhana" on the left cheek; "to Agni Aśvodaraja" on the liṅga; "to Agni Vaiśvānara" on the right cheek; "to Agni Kauśaratejas" on the right side; "to Agni Viśvamukha" on the right nostril; and "O God Agni, protect me" on the left nostril—having thus performed the placement of the eight forms (aṣṭamūrti), one should prepare a seat within the circle in the center of the fire and place the pedestal (pīṭha) with the mantra: "To Ādhāraśakti."

To Prakṛti (0), to Kūrma (0), to Ananta (0), to Varāha (0), to Pṛthivī (0), to the Ocean of Milk (0), to Śvetadvīpa (0), to Mahīmeru (0), to Ratnamaṇḍapa (0), to Kalpavṛkṣa (0), to Ratnavedikā (0), to Ratnasiṃhāsana (0). To Dakṣa (right) Dharmā (0) and Vāmā (0) [at] Jñāna (0); to Gama (0) and Rau (0) [at] Vairāgya (0); to Dakṣa (right) and Aurau (0) Īśvaryā (0). Thus are the pedestal-feet starting from the southeast corner. At the mouth, on the left side, [is] A... [the rest of the text is incomplete].

At the hub of the wheel of knowledge (*jñānāra*), for the sake of sovereignty (*aiśvarya*) on the right side, [one offers] to Ananta, who is endowed with a thousand hoods and a continuous girdle in the middle of the limbs of the seats starting from the southeast (*āgneya*). Above the hood in the center of that, [one offers] to the bulb of bliss (*ānandakanda*), to the stalk of consciousness (*saṃvinnāla*), to the lotus consisting of all principles (*sarvatattvātmakapadma*), to the petals which are *prakṛti*, to the filaments which are the *vikāras*, and finally to the pericarp enriched with the fifty seed-syllables (*bīja*).

In the center of the lotus: *āṃ* to the solar maṇḍala consisting of twelve kalās; *īṃ* to the lunar maṇḍala consisting of sixteen kalās; *uṃ* to the fire maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās; *saṃ* to Sattva, the essence of awakening; *raṃ* to Rajas, the essence of activity; *taṃ* to Tamas, the essence of delusion. To its right: *ā* to the Ātman; to the west: *ā* to the Antarātman; to the north: *yaṃ* to the Parātman; to the east: *jñāṃ* to the Jñānātman; and in the center: *māṃ* to the Tattvātman.

Having placed [the syllables] *kaṃ*, *kala*, *tattvāya*, *vi*, *vidhā*, *tattvāya*, *paṃ*, *para*, *tattvāya* one by one upon the eight petals and the pericarp, one should contemplate the nine powers (*navashakti*) in a clockwise direction starting from the east: *oṃ pītāyai*, *śvetāyai*, *aruṇāyai*, *kṛṣṇāyai*, *dhūmrāyai*, *tīvrāyai*, *syuliṅginītyai*, *rucirāyai*, and in the center, *jvālinyai*. Right there, [one should contemplate] Vaiśvānara, Jātavedas, Havyavāha, and Lohita.

*Tākṣasarvakarmāṇi sādhaya svāhā* (0). Having worshipped thus with *agnimūrtiyogapīṭhāśanāya* (0), one should meditate: "One should meditate upon Fire (Vahni)—the desired Śakti—resplendent with the Svastika and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhayamudrā*), possessing the luster of the Japā flower, adorned with golden ornaments, stationed within the sacrificial post (*yama*), three-eyed, wearing a crown of matted locks, and with his head bound. (1) Having meditated thus, and having displayed the mudrās of the [five] powers (*vara*, *śakti*, *svastika*, *abhaya*, and the six tongues), one should perform the *anvādāna* (preliminary offering). In this [rite], there is the *Caṇḍī* [mantra].

While performing the oblation (*homa*), for the purpose of securing the deities, I shall perform the *anvādhāna* (preparation of the fire). Having recited from "In this consecrated fire... up to "...the eyes with clarified butter (*ājya*)," I shall perform the primary oblations: nine offerings to the Nine Planets (*navagraha*) with the aforementioned substances in the aforementioned number; likewise, [oblations] with the aforementioned substances for the *mūlamantra*—which consists of the *sāvarṇi* mantra beginning with "Sūryatanaya" and ending with "Sāvarṇir bhavitā manuputra," combined with the *mālāmantra* consisting of ten repetitions of the nine *caṇḍī* verses; and likewise, one repetition each for the deities of the enclosures (*varaṇadevatā*).

Having offered clarified butter (*ājya*) with the formula "I shall sacrifice to Śeṣa with the remainder as *Sviṣṭakṛt*," and so on three times, ending with "to Agni and the Maruts with *ājya*" and "to Aṃśu and the Maruts with *ājya*"; [he offers] to Viṣṇu, the Lord of the Pitṛs, the Gandharvas, the Puṣkas, the Nāgas, and the Piśācas—these deities presiding over the *rasanā*s—with *ājya*. From the oblation for the eyes and other organs, he offers twenty-five oblations with the *Śūla* mantra using *ājya*. To the Viśvedevas, the Saṃsāvas, the limb-deities (*aṅgadevatās*), and the principal deity, he offers with *ājya*.

Having worshipped all the deities of the *pīṭha*, the deities of the pavilion, and their respective attendants, one should offer this [oblation] upon the upper girdle (*mekhalā*) with the mantra "idaṃ viṣṇuḥ"; upon the middle girdle, which is red, one should worship Viṣṇu; upon the middle girdle, which is red, one should worship Brahmā with the mantra "brahma jajñānam"; upon the lower girdle, one should worship Rudra with the mantra "kadrudrāya"; and upon the lower girdle, which is red, one should worship Gaurī with the mantra "gaurīrmimāya. Then, having performed the sweeping of the ground and the rites up to the consecration of the clarified butter (*ājya-saṃskāra*), one should proceed with darbha grass that is devoid of internal nodes.

Having spread [the materials] upon the middle girdle and cast them into the directions starting from the east, one should worship Brahmā for Viṣṇu, Rudra, and Īśvara. Having worshipped Gaurī at the yoni with the mantra: "O Vaiśvānara, Jātavedas, Bahulohitākṣa, accomplish all rites, svāhā," and having honored [Him] with perfumes and flowers, one should employ those respective [mantras] such as the Śāntika and others in the mouth of the fire, within the hexagon, proceeding clockwise from the center.

Having worshipped the goddesses Hāhā, Prahāsa, Guptā, and Sajihvā, one should worship [the deity] upon the filaments of the eight-petaled lotus outside of that, in the directions of Agni, Īśāna, Asura, Vāyu, and the center, with the mantra beginning "sahasrārciṣe," and so forth. Then, on the petals starting from the eastern tip and proceeding clockwise, one should worship the eight forms [of Śiva] beginning with Agni Jātavedas. Next, in the four corners, one should worship Indra and the others with their respective name-mantras, and having worshipped the weapons outside of that, [one worships] Nirṛti and the rest.

Having sprinkled [the ghee] with the *aprabhūta* mantra, or having taken it from the house if it has not yet been prepared, one should remove the embers to the north with the *namaḥ* mantra. Having poured clarified butter (*ājya*) into the water-vessel with the *astra* mantra, and having consecrated it eight times with the root mantra, one should transform it into nectar by means of the *dhenu-mudrā* while reciting "vaṃ. Then, with blazing *darbha* grass while reciting "huṃ," one should perform the *nīrājana* (circumambulation) of the ghee therein. After casting the *darbha* blades into the fire, one should kindle fresh *darbha* blades and, with the *astra* mantra, sprinkle the ghee toward each of the directions within the fire.

Having cast [the materials] and purified them with the *namaḥ* mantra, having placed them in the fire, and then having performed the *niṣkaṇḍaka* oblations with the *Savitṛ* mantra, having performed the rites from the spreading of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) up to the *cakṣuṣya* offering, and having established the *sruc* and *sruva* ladles upon the western sacrificial grass— or, in their absence, having taken two leaves of the *palāśa* tree— and having heated them over the fire, wiped them with *darbha* grass while reciting "hum," consecrated them with the *astra* mantra, sprinkled them, and placed them upon the *darbha* grass; thus [is the preparation of] the *sruc*.

Taking clarified butter with the *sruva* ladle from the *pitṛtaḥ* vessel, one should offer it into the right eye of the fire with "Agnaye svāhā," saying "This is for Agni, obeisance. Taking it again, one offers it into the left eye with "Somāya svāhā," saying "This is for Soma, obeisance. Taking it again, one offers it into the third eye of the fire with "Agnoṣomābhyāṃ svāhā," saying "This is for Agni and Soma, obeisance. Taking it again, one should offer it into the mouth of the fire with "Agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā," saying "This is for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, obeisance. Then: "Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā—this is for Agni; bhuvaḥ svāhā vauṣaṭ—this is for Vāyu; svāhā..."

Having offered four oblations with "Hā sūrye-pedaṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ svāhā Prajāpataye idaṃ," and having offered three oblations with the Vaiśvānara mantra, one should make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "I offer eight oblations with the *praṇava* for the sake of accomplishing the fifteen sacraments (*saṃskāras*) beginning with conception (*garbhādhāna*) and ending with marriage, as well as the established rites. Then, having offered eight times with "Oṃ, I perform the meditation on the conception of this fire, svāhā," one proceeds in the same manner for each subsequent sacrament.

The rites are as follows: (1) *puṃsavana*, (2) *sīmanta-nayana*, (3) *jātakarman*, (4) *nāmakaraṇa*—you are named Śatamaṅgala—(5) *niṣkramaṇa*, (6) *annaprāśana*, (7) *cūḍākaraṇa*, (8) *upanayana*, (9) *mahānāmnī*, (10) *mahāvrata*, (11) *upaniṣad*, (12) *godāna*, (13) *samāvartana*, and (14) *vivāha*. These are the purificatory rites (*saṃskāra*) for auspicious acts; however, for cruel acts, there is (15) death. Then, five...

Having taken the *casami* fuel and offered oblations into the fires with the root-mantra of ignorance (*avidyā*) as the base, one should then offer individual oblations of clarified butter (*ājya*) to the deities of the tongue-forms, saying: "Svāhā to the immortals" (1), "Svāhā to the ancestors" (2), "Svāhā to the gandharvas" (3), "Svāhā to the yakṣas" (4), "Svāhā to the nāgas" (5), "Svāhā to the piśācas" (6), and "Svāhā to the rākṣasas" (7). Then, [one offers]: "Oṃ Svāhā," "Śrīṃ Svāhā" (2), "Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Svāhā" (3), and "Oṃ Śrīṃ... (4).

*Hrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* (4) *Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ svāhā* (5) *Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ svāhā* (6) *Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye svāhā* (8) *Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me svāhā* (9) *Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā svāhā svāhā* (10). Thus [ends] the Śrī Mahāgaṇa...
Having divided the mantra ten times and offered oblations, one should again offer oblations four times with the entire mantra: *oṃ śrī svāhā* (4).

Then, having offered a single oblation of clarified butter (*ājya*) with the previously mentioned fire-mantra: *oṃ vaisvā sādhave vauṣaṭ svāhā*, and having thus consecrated the fire, one should meditate upon the Deity therein.

Having worshipped [the Deity] with the nine-syllable mantra using perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, and having contemplated the identity (*aikya*) of the fire and the Deity, [one performs] the "mouth-opening" (*agnimukha*) rite. Then...

Oṃ: Having performed the homa with the substances prescribed for the nine planets (*navagraha*) in the stated quantities, as well as the previously mentioned substances, using the *Saptashati* mantra beginning with the letter *Sa* and ending with the letter *Na* as the middle mantra in its divided form; and having offered one thousand oblations into the fire of Caṇḍī—if there is an insufficiency of daily offerings—by casting some small amount of offering substance into the clarified butter (*ghṛta*); thus having completed the principal homa, one should offer clarified butter to the deities of the sacrifice with their respective name-mantras: Oṃ U...

*Vrahmaṇe svāhā*. Thus [recite] everywhere: *Oṃ Aryamṇe*, *Vivasvate*, *Mitrāya*, *Pṛthvīdharāya*, *Savitṛ-Sāvitṛbhyām*, *Vibudhādhipa-Jayābhyām*, *Rāja-Pakṣma-Rudrābhyām*, *Āpa-Apavatsābhyām*, *Śikhine*, *Paryanyāya*, *Jayantāya*, *Kuliśāyudhāya*, *Sūryāya*, *Satyāya*, *Bhaśāya*, *Ākāśāya*. In the northwest: *Pūṣṇe*, *Vitathāya*, *Gṛhakṣatāya*.
To Yama, to Pārṣṇi, to Gandharva, to Śṛṅgarāja, to the Pitṛs, to Dauvārika, to Sugrīva, to Puṣpadanta, to Varuṇa, to Asura,

To Pilipicchā, [offer] a very firm gateway; to Rāhu and Bṛhaspati, a gateway of Subhadra for Dhruva; to Sūrya and Aṅgāraka, a gateway of Sukarma for Dhara; to Śukra and Budha, a gateway of Suhotra for Vākpati; to Soma, Ketu, and Śani; to Vighneśa; to Airāvata; to Indra; to Kṣetrapāla; to Vighnanāśana; to Kṣetrapālabhairava; to Mahāla...

To Nidhi and Vasumatī; to Gaṇeśa; to Kṣetreśa; to Gaṇadevī; to Yamunā; to Dhātṛ; to Dehalī; to Kāma; Oṃ, to Deva; to Vasanta; to Yama; to Daṇḍa; to Kumuda; to Durjaya. To the twelve Ādityas; to the Aśvins; to the Viśvedevas who possess the side of truth; to the Gandharvas and Apsarases; to Skanda; to the Bull (Vṛṣabha); to Durgā; to Viṣṇu; to Svadhā; to Death and Diseases; to Gaṇapati; to the Waters; to the Earth; to the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā; to the seven oceans; to the Mace (Gadā) in the mouth; to the Trident (Triśūla); to the Thunderbolt (Vajra); to the Spear (Śakti); to the Staff (Daṇḍa); to the Sword (Khaḍga); to the Noose (Pāśa); to the Goad (Aṅkuśa); to Gautama; to Bharadvāja; to Viśvāmitra; to Kaśyapa; to Atri; to Ja...

Salutations to Agni, Vasiṣṭha, Aṃrudhanī, Indrī, Kaumārya, Brāhmī, Vārāhī, Cāmuṇḍā, Vaiṣṇavī, Māheśvarī, Vaināyakī, Sūrya, Soma, Bhauma, Budha, Guru, Śukra, Śanaiścara, Rāhu, Ketu, Ambikā, Gaurī, Skanda, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Indra,
Yama, Kāla, Citragupta, Agni, Aditi, Bhūmi, Viṣṇu, Indra, Indrāṇī, and Prajāpati. Svāhā.
To the serpents, to Brahmā, to Gaṇapati, to Durgā, to Kṣetrapāla, to Vāyu, to Āśā, and to the two Aśvins.

To the Mothers of the Gods (Devamātṛs), to Bhadrakālī, to Sarasvatī, to Gaurī, to the divine [beings] (Divyauḍyas), to the Siddhas, to the Goddess Śubhaṅkarī, to Gaurī, to the divine [beings], to the Siddhas, to the human [beings] (Mānavauḍyas), to Sarasvatī, to Mahālakṣmī, to Gaurī, to the divine [beings], to the Siddhas, to the human [beings], to Māyādevī, to Durgā, to Diśimā, to the Western Door (Paścimadvāra), to the Jewel-Pavilion (Ratnamaṇḍapa), to Vāstu...
To Ruṣāya, to Vāstvadhīśvara-Brahman, to Kulanātha, to Śrī Dīpanātha joined with the twelve red Śaktis, to Puraṃdarī, to Vādikyāntā, to Viśinīdiṅmātrā the messenger, to Vādiṅmātrā, to Sumukhī,
to Vitayā, to Vimalā, to Puṣpāranyā, to Vadaryā, to Sundarī, and to Vādiṅmātrā.

Salutation to Mātṛkā, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Rudra, Gaurī, and Brahmā; to one’s own month; to Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Dhruva, Dhara, Soma, the Waters, Anila, Prabha, Uṣas, Prabhāsa, and the eleven Rudras;
to Vāstoṣpati; to the seven lunar mansions beginning with Aśvinī; to the seven yogas beginning with Viṣkambha; and to the two karaṇas, Vava and Bālava.

To the *ptadīpa*s; to the *Ṛgveda*; to the seven constellations beginning with Puṣya; to the seven yogas beginning with Dhṛti; to the seven yogas beginning with Vajra; to the two karaṇas, Gara and Vaṇija;

to the seven netherworlds (*pātāla*s); to the *Sāmaveda*; to the seven constellations beginning with Abhijit; to the six yogas beginning with Sādhya; to the *Viṣṭi* karaṇa; to the seven worlds beginning with Bhūḥ; to the *Atharvaveda*; to Dhruva; to the seven sages (*ṛṣi*s); to the Gaṅgā and others...

One hundred and eight pieces of fuel for the seven great mountain ranges (kulācalas); eight for the Vasus; twelve for the Ādityas; eleven for the Rudras; forty-nine for the Maruts; sixteen for the Mothers (mātṛs); six for the Seasons (ṛtus); twelve for the Months; two for each of the two solstices (ayanas); fifteen for the lunar days (tithis); sixty for the years;
[and offerings] for the Suparṇas, the Nāgas, the Bhūris, the Pakṣas, the Gandharvas, and humans; thereafter, the *pūrṇāhuti*.

Having performed the oblation according to the previously established sequence starting from Ṛccharṇagiri and the sacred seats (pīṭhas) up to the lunar mandala, and then having offered individual oblations of clarified butter (ājyāhuti) to the sacred seats and the Gurus beginning with "Obeisance to the Gurus" (gurubhyo namaḥ) up to Ṛddhi; and then, having honored the deities of the enclosures (āvaraṇadevatās) in the order they were written, beginning from Nanda up to Cakrāyudha, having offered one oblation of clarified butter for each, [one should offer]: "To Bhūḥ, to Agni, and to the Great Earth, Svāhā! To Bhuvaḥ, to Vāyu, and to the Atmosphere..."

Having offered four oblations of clarified butter with the mantras: "To Kṣaya and Mahat, Svāhā! To Suvar and Āditya and Div and Mahat, Svāhā! To Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ and Candramas and Nakṣatras and Diśas and Mahat, Svāhā!"—and then having offered the *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation with "To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, Svāhā!", and having offered the binding of the fuel-sticks (*idhma*) and so forth, as well as the *marutvatīya* and *ājyena* offerings, [he recites]: "Oṃ, O Lord of the Gods..."

Having offered twenty-five oblations of clarified butter with the *tat-savitur-vareṇyam* mantra to the ancestors (*pitṛ*), the *gandharvas*, the *pathaukṣas*, the *nāgas*, the *piśācas*, and the *rākṣasas*, and having offered the *saṃsrāva* (the residue of the oblation) with the mantra "To the Viśvedevas, Svāhā!", [he recites]: "Om! Whatever [sin] was committed by me here previously—whether through the authority of my vital breaths (*prāṇa*), intellect (*buddhi*), body (*deha*), or sense-faculties (*dhātu*)—in the states of waking (*jāgrat*), dreaming (*svapna*), and deep sleep (*suṣupta*), whether by mind (*manas*), speech (*vāc*), hands (*hastābhyām*), action (*karmaṇā*), the thighs (*ūru*), the belly (*udareṇa*), or the generative organ (*śiśnā*), that which was touched..."

Having offered eight oblations of clarified butter with the mantra: *kṛtaṃ yakṛtaṃ tat sarvaṃ brahmārpaṇaṃ bhavatu svāhā*, and having offered one oblation with the mantra: *oṃ nyūnātirikta-siddhy-artham dadāmi sa-ghṛtaṃ tilaṃ oṃ sāgaṃ kuru svāhā*, [one should perform] the procedure for the expiatory oblation (*prāyaścitta-homa*). Then, having made the offering of sacrificial food (*bali*) starting from Indra and ending with Kṣetrapāla, and having likewise performed the offering of sacrificial food for the planets and others, [one should offer] black gram (*māṣa*) to the Goddess.

One should offer the food-oblation (*bhakta-bali*) before the Goddess with the mantra: *mūlānte mahātyai imaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa mama sarvāpachāntiṃ kuru svāhā*. Thus one should give the oblation to the Goddess. Then, having duly offered the oblations starting from Nandaja up to Bhrānti, one should offer outside of that to the east the oblation to Gaṇapati with: *gaṇapataye imaṃ baliṃ samarpayāmi namaḥ*. To the south, [one offers] the oblation to Kṣetrapāla. Then, [the oblation to] the sixty-four Yoginīs...

One should offer the *bali* to the [deities] beginning with *Bhyaḥ*. Alternatively, having established sixteen *bali*-offerings in the four directions, one should offer the *bali* in the sequence starting from the east with the mantra:

*Oṃ jape 'mbai maṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa yajamānasya īpsitaṃ kuru kuru svāhā*. In this manner, one should offer the *bali* as before, using the mantras beginning with "Vijaye" and ending with "Viṣalambinī," or those ending in the word "vrya. Then, having offered *bali* to the nine planets (*navagraha*) and the weapons (*astra*) by means of their respective name-mantras, it is thus concluded.

To a Brāhmaṇa, one should give black gram (*māṣa*), cooked rice (*bhakti*), *kuṣmāṇḍa* (pumpkin gourd), coconut, *viphala* fruit, and sugarcane. To Kṣatriyas and others, one should not give any of these; rather, one should give one of the following: a buffalo, a ram, a goat, or a boar. One should not give the meat of a female animal, because there is even a slight prohibition against it. Now follows the procedure for the offering (*bali*) of a goat and so forth: having proclaimed the place and time, [one says], "I, of such-and-such lineage and such-and-such name, for the great pleasure of..."
Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*), "I shall offer this goat as a sacrificial gift (*balī*)," the performer, facing north, places the sacrificial offering before the goddess who faces east;

holding it at her left ear, he should recite this mantra: "Salutations to you, who have the form of a beast, whose self is dear to all beings; salutations to the King of Beasts, the witness, whose nature encompasses the beginning, the middle, and the end. Having thus offered obeisance three times with this mantra, he should seize the beast from the northwest (the *vāyavya* direction) with the first [mantra].

One should perform the circumambulation from the right; one should offer the animal with the mantra "by the wheel" (*cakreṇa*) as the second [circumambulation], and "may we be together" (*samāḥ syāma*) as the third. Having thus circumambulated three times, saying "O Vāta, do not strike" (*ā vāta vāhi*), and having recited the root mantra beginning with "the vital breath is indeed Vāta, food is the root," one should offer some food.

Then, taking hold of the uncut [portion] with the left hand, one offers it three times with the mantra "to the terrible ones" (*ghorebhyaḥ*) and "shine forth, *hum*" (*uddīpyasva huṃ*). Having offered it, one takes hold of the uncut [portion] with the left hand, [reciting] "to the terrible ones" (*ghorebhyaḥ*).

Then, having recited the mantra "Uddīpyasva huṃ itīt na," one should sprinkle the unborn goat (aja). [O] Karahrī, Yamunā, Gaṅgā, Karatoyā, Sarasvatī, Kāverī, Candrabhāgā, Asi, Sindhu, Bhairava, and Sāgara: O Maheśāni, provide here the necessary means for the bathing of the goat. For the destruction of the bonds of the bound soul (paśu), [I offer this] to the one residing on Mount Hemakuṭa, to the Supreme, to the Parameṣṭhin, and to the Form of the syllable Huṃ. [Recite] "Sahasraśīrṣā" three times.

Having sprinkled himself with water from the *ajā* (goat-skin) vessel, and having cast drops of perfume, flowers, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), and the special *arghya* water upon a flower, he should recite the *karasaṃpuṭa* mantra:

"Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! O Śiva, this is the clarified butter (ghee), this is the *piṇḍa*; therefore, attain the state of Śiva. Wake up! You are indeed Śiva. O Śiva, you have been brought here for the sake of the work of Śiva by the command of Śiva. [This should be recited] into the right ear.

Oṃ! You, the goat, have been instructed; by my good fortune you have appeared here in the form of Bali. I always bow with devotion to you who possess form and who take the form of Bali, through the offering that grants pleasure to Caṇḍikā and destroys the misfortune of the donor. O Bali, salutations again and again to you, who are the very form of the sacrificial offering to Caṇḍikā. "Beasts were created by the Self-born One himself for the sake of sacrifice; therefore, I do not kill you, for killing in this way is no killing. Having thus consecrated [the victim] with the mantra *aiṃ hrīṃ*...

Having cast flowers with the mantra *Śrīṃ iti* and so forth, and having offered water with the words, "I offer this *bali* for the pleasure of Caṇḍikā to [Name] of such-and-such lineage and [Name]-śarman," one should then perform the purification of the sword (*khaḍga*). Having brought the sword before oneself, worshipped it with perfumes and flowers using the mantra *Oṃ khaḍgāya*, and having smeared it with red sandalwood and vermilion, one should meditate upon it as black, holding a bow, and having the form of the Night of Doom (*Kālarātri*).

Having meditated thus: "The one with a face and eyes red like molten copper, adorned with red garlands and unguents, wearing red garments, holding a noose and a club, a householder drinking blood, devouring a multitude of riches"—and having offered a handful of flowers while saying, "O tongue of Caṇḍikā, you who adorn the world of the gods, be forever gracious; having cut the sacrificial offering (bali), grant me a boon," [one recites]: *oṃ hrīṃ khaṇḍgakāli vajraśarīra lohadaṇḍāya ī*.

Having written the seed-syllables *jāliṃ*, *ba*, *dhvā*, *khaḍga*, and *kūrca* with red sandalwood paste and other substances, and having paid homage with "Oṃ hrīṃ devyai namaḥ," one should recite with palms joined in prayer: "O Sword, you are the bestower of weapons, a blade of sharp edge, difficult to approach, the womb of prosperity, and the seed of victory; salutations to you who protect the Dharma! Having thus offered this prayer, one should consecrate the offering to the deity with the root mantra: Oṃ hrīṃ (twice) kālī (twice) kaṭadaṃṣṭe spho (twice) phetkāriṇī.

"Khādaya (2) chedayata (2) sarvaduṣṭān māraya (2) imam amuka-liṅgin-chindhi (2) kiṭikiṭi rudhiraṃ piba (2) sphro (2) kili (2) kāli (2) svāhā (2). Having thus consecrated it, one should employ it against Bala and Skanda. Reciting "Ā hūṃ phaṭ," one should employ it against Skanda; then, one should recite the Gāyatrī at the right ear: "Paphaḍ-pāśāya vidmahe vipra-kīr-gāyatrīmahi; tanno jī pracodayāt."

Having instructed thus, one should sever [the victim] with the *paśupatāstra* mantra, striking the neck with a sword. As stated in the *Rudrayāmala*: "Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ, O Kauśikī, be satiated with blood! Having offered the oblation (*bali*) to the Goddess with the mantra "Oṃ yatāmi," one should take the remainder of the offering with the following mantra: "Oṃ sphurad-kumbha-sūnu-guru-dhanu-māraya vidāraya vidrāvaya kaṃpaya kaṃpātaya pūraya oṃ hrīḥ oṃ huṃ phaṭ hūṃ pharda. Then, having lit a lamp before that head of the Goddess...
Then, one should offer the remainder outside; therein the mantras are: "May these gods receive the bali-offering:

the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Maruts, the two Aśvins, the Rudras, the Suparṇas, the Pannagas, the Grahas, the Asuras, the Yatudhānas, the Piśācas, the Uragas, the Rākṣasas, the Ḍākinīs, the Yakṣas, the Vetālas, the Yoginīs, the Pūtanās, the Śivās, the Jṛmbhakas, the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, the Mahā-vidyādharas and their followers, the Guardians of the Quarters (Dikpālas), and the Protectors of the Worlds (Lokapālas)."
May the obstacles and Vināyakas be appeased; may Brahmā and the other great sages, who bring peace to the worlds, grant me no obstacle and destroy my sin and adversaries.
May the spirits and ghosts (bhūta-preta) become gentle, satisfied, and bringers of happiness. Those who are fierce, performers of fierce deeds, and dwellers in fierce places;
the Yoginīs of terrible form; and those who are lords of the Gaṇas—whether they move on earth, in the sky, or in the intermediate space—may all of them be pleased.

"O beings who have become [manifest] in the mind, accept this bali! Having offered this bali and taken handfuls of flowers, may all those beings who dwell upon the earth, having received this bali offered according to the rules, attain satisfaction and depart; may they forgive me. There is no other [debt]; salutations to them! Having thus offered the handful of flowers and recited "The Earth," one should perform the rite of peace (śānti). Then, having released [the ritual focus], washed his hands and feet, and prepared the full vessel (pūrṇapātra) and so forth outside, he should proceed.

Having performed the rite ending with *apītha*, and having worshipped [the fire] with the mantra *agnaye nayi*, he should pray: "Salutations to you, the thousand-rayed one of great splendor, who assumes many forms; salutations to you, the all-consuming, omnipresent purifier. You are Raudra; you are the destroyer of fierce desires; salutations to you. You are Viṣṇu, you are the protector of the world; grant us peace. Having thus prayed to Agni, he should then fill the *sruc* with twelve portions taken by means of the *sruva*.

Having placed [the vessel] containing coconut and other items, along with sandalwood and other substances, upon it, the Ācārya—while the sacrificer maintains contact with him—should offer the *pūrṇāhuti* (full oblation) with the triplet beginning "samudrād ūmiḥ," the single verse "mūrdhānaṃ divaḥ," the single verse "punastvā," the single verse "pūrṇā darvi," the verse "sapta te agne," the verse "dhāmaṃ te," and the root mantra. Having offered the *pūrṇāhuti*, [he recites]: "This [is for] Agni Vaiśvānara, the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, [and] for a hundred..."

"Obeisance to Agni who has entered the sequence, and obeisance to Mahālakṣmī"—thus [he should say]. Then, having offered the *vasordhārā* oblation, the procedure there is as follows: having fixed two pillars above the fire, one should place a straight branch of the *udumbara* tree, as thick as the forearm and with its tip facing east; upon that, a vessel (*kuṃbha*) supported by a girdle (*mekhalā*), filled with clarified butter (*ghṛta*), should be placed so that it has an opening of about a barley-corn (*yava*) at the bottom. As the clarified butter is released through that opening from above, it flows down until it reaches the bottom, which is likewise about a barley-corn in thickness.

Through the opening of the *sruva* ladle, one should cause the clarified butter (*ājya*) to fall from above into that vessel containing the ghee. While it is thus held over the fire with a golden needle, one should recite the mantras.

One should recite the mantra beginning with "agnim īḷe" and ending with "divas pṛthivyā uta. Again, having filled the *sruk* ladle and placed a fruit and flower upon it, one should cover its opening with the downward-turned mouth [of the other ladle], grasp them together with both hands like a hollowed vessel, and [recite] the root mantra.

Having offered an oblation with "vauṣaṭ" and "svāhā," and having performed the worship of the fire by spreading the sacrificial grass (paristaraṇa) around it and completing the ritual recitation (japa), one should worship the pedestal (pīṭha) and the deity with the fivefold offerings (pañcopacāra). Then, having praised her with the hymn beginning with "khaṇḍginī śūlinī," followed by the four verses beginning with "śūlena śūlapāhinī devī," the five verses beginning with "namo devyai," and the five verses beginning with "sarvasvarūpe śarve," and having prostrated and offered a handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali), one should pray as follows: rū... [text truncated]

"O Paṇḍehiyasāśodā, O Bhagavatī, give me a son, give me wealth, and grant me all my desires. O slayer of Mahiṣa, O Great Māyā, O Cāmuṇḍā, O Mālinī, O Āyārā, O Goddess, grant me health and sovereignty; salutations to you. Having thus offered salutation, the preceptor (ācārya) and others should perform the rite for the attainment of welfare. Then, having given a seat to the preceptor and having placed the water from the ritual jar (kalaśa) into another vessel, [he should perform] the consecration (abhiṣeka).

Having been thus consecrated, the couple should bathe and put on other garments. Then, having performed the inspection of the clarified butter (*ājya*) in a bell-metal vessel, and having given [gifts] to the Brahmins, they should worship the Fire and also worship the Planets. Having prayed: "O Fire, O Great Power, you who bestow the fruits of all actions, when this other rite has arrived, please remain present with great respect," and having thus made the petition, one should then dismiss the Goddess with: "Arise! (uttiṣṭha).
"O Lord of the Earth, you are present in these two [hands]. O Goddess, arise! O Goddess Cāmuṇḍā, having accepted this auspicious worship, bestow upon me well-being along with your eight Śaktis.
Having thus performed the withdrawal with the *saṃhāramudrā* and personally dismissed [the deity], one should then raise the *nirmālya* (the remains of the offering):
"Go, go to the supreme abode, your own station, O Goddess Caṇḍikā! Proceed to the waters of the ocean; rise up, shaking the mountain with your hand! O Goddess Durgā, protect the world!"
"O worshipful Mother of the Three Worlds, go to your own abode. When the year has passed, for the sake of my return, please accept this increasing worship offered by me according to my capacity;

taking it with you for the purpose of protection, go to your supreme abode. Having said this, one should cast [the image] into flowing water. In the case of the *Caṇḍī-śata* and other rites, after the *homa*, the ritual dismissal (*udvāsana*) should be performed as before: "O Mother of the Three Worlds, O Goddess, endowed with compassion for all beings, be well-pleased by this gift."

Thus ends the prayer for the *navarātra*. Regarding the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*): for a *śata-caṇḍī*, it is one *niṣka*; for each subsequent ten-fold increase, up to a *lakṣa-caṇḍī*, the fee increases tenfold.

For those who are unable [to give so much], gold and a cow [should be given]. Then, having given the fee to the gate-keepers (*dvāra-jāpaka*) and others, and having offered food to Brahmins and married women (*suvāsinī*) for the sake of accomplishing the completeness of the rite, and having given a water-pot (*muḍapa*) to the Preceptor (*ācārya*), one should perform the propitiation of the Lord of the Rite (*karmeśvara-aryana*). [This is] the eternal [instruction] of Vimalānandanātha.

Thus ends the thirteenth wave in the *Tārābhaktitaraṅgiṇī*, composed with a single-minded devotion to Tārā by the venerable Vimalānandanātha. This concludes the thirteenth wave, titled "The Exposition of the Ritual Manual for the Worship, Fire-offerings (*homa*), and Other Rites pertaining to the Navacaṇḍī, Śatacaṇḍī, and Sahasracaṇḍī. Now, the rites for specific desires (*kāmyakarmāṇi*) are described. Among these, since all rites for specific desires result in fruits...

The *daughata-argalayantra* is now described as it was taught in the *Śāradātilaka*: "Having drawn the eight directional bolts (*digargala*), one should write the mantra of three syllables within the [central] square;

in the other [surrounding] squares, one should write the two eight-syllable mantras. Having written the six syllables beginning with *aku* and ending with *para*, and the pair *yuga*, *la*, *ya*, *va*, *ra*, *anyo*, and *māsa* upon the bolts (*argala*), then, characterized by the qualities of Varuṇa and the others, one should draw two rows [of syllables]. Beyond that, in the corners, one should place the eight-syllable mantra together with the Self."

One should write the *māyā* (the letter *ī*) situated within the pair of vowels (*ā* and *ī*) in the filaments and petals; the root mantra in three rows; encircled three times by the letters entwined with the noose (*pāśa*) and goad (*aṅkuśa*); and surrounded in sequence by the jar-mouthed lotus at the top. Outside of that, one should draw the *raghāṭārgala* diagram, which is the secret gift for practitioners. The first eight-syllable mantra is: *parā śrīśakti kadarpakāmaśaktīdirāṅkuśāḥ*. Then: *kāmini rañjini svāhā*.
Another mantra of eighteen syllables is proclaimed: *Māyā-gaurī-rudra-dayite-yogīśvarī*, followed by *yacchandaṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.

Thus, O Goddess, this sixteen-syllable mantra is described. Furthermore, in the *Prakāyā* [Tantra], it is said: "The eight [syllables] within the peaceful [state], joined with *galā-vihaṃla-vara*, preceded and followed by *caṭakaṃ koṣṭa-ghat-svāṅga*, known as the pair of eight syllables, and outside [that] the pair of *ātman* joined with *māyā*."

The lotus has filaments that meet at the center and petals with eyes; its middle is adorned by three rows of petals, and its sides shine with the goad (*aṅkuśa*) and noose (*pāśa*). Encircled by goads and nooses, it is formed by letters moving in both direct and reverse order, fashioned within the enclosure of a lotus. That very [lotus] is yellowish, bestowing desired fruits and auspiciousness, and is called the "Moon-Supreme" (*caṃdrotama*); thus it is in the center of the *ghaṭārgala*. Now, the method for constructing that diagram is stated: from east to west...
Having drawn two long lines with a space between them, and likewise two lines of that same dimension to the south and north,

and likewise two lines of that same dimension to the southwest and northeast, and likewise two lines of that same dimension to the northwest and southeast; having drawn these in a long form, one should make a circle in their center, and within that, [draw] the *hṛllekhā* mantra containing the name of the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*), accompanied by the *pāśa* and *aṅkuśa* seed-syllables situated on its two sides.

Having inscribed the six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅga-mantra*) in the eight triangles adjacent to that [central triangle] and having written the enclosure of the limbs (*aṅgāvaraṇa*), one should then draw a circle outside of that such that sixteen squares are formed. Within those sixteen squares, one should write the sixteen-syllable mantra of the Śakti. Outside of that, one should make some lines; when this is done, the space between the two lines takes the form of a bolt (*argala*). On the eastern bolt, one writes: *lhalhāṃ lhiṃ lhīṃ huluṃ lhū*.

One should write the row *ktiṃ liṃ* on the western bolt (*paścimārgale*). Likewise, one should write the row *lhaḥ aiṃ lhoṃ lhauṃ lhaṃḥ* on the south-eastern bolt (*āgneyārgale*). Likewise, one should write the row *ha saṃ hasāṃ hsāṃ hsiṃ hsīṃ hsūṃ hsūṃ* on the north-western bolt (*vāyavyārgale*). Likewise, [one should write] *hseṃ hsaiṃ hsoṃ hsauṃ hsaṃ hsaḥ* on the [other bolt].

One should write the row: *vhaṃ vhaṃ vhiṃ vhuṃ vhaṃ vhaḥ*. Then, on the southern bolt (*dakṣiṇārgala*), one should write the row: *vheṃ vhaiṃ vhoṃ v hauṃ vhaṃ vhaḥ*. Likewise, on the southwestern bolt (*naiṛtyārgala*), one should write the row: *hraṃ hrāṃ hriṃ hrīṃ hraḥ*. Similarly, on the northeastern bolt (*īśānārgala*), one should write the row:
*hreṃ hraiṃ hroṃ hrauṃ hraḥ*. Having done that, having opened [the diagram], one should draw eight petals; there, upon those petals, [one should place] *ahaṃ*.

One should write [the syllables] in this sequence: *saḥ iṃhaṃsaḥ*, *āṃhaṃsaḥ*, *iṃhaṃsaḥ*, *uṃhaṃsaḥ*, *īṃhaṃsaḥ*, *ūṃhaṃsaḥ*, *ṛṃhaṃsaḥ*, *īhaṃsaḥ*, *ḷhaṃsaḥ*, *īhaṃsaḥ*, *ḹṃ haṃsaḥ*, *eṃhaṃsaḥ*, *īhaṃsaḥ*, *aiṃhaṃsaḥ*, *ohaṃsaḥ*, *īhaṃsaḥ*, *aṃhaṃsaḥ*, *aḥhaṃsaḥ*.
Having written the three lines of the *hṛllekhā* mantra, separated by the *pāśa* and *aṅkuśa* mantras, in the middle of each petal, one should then draw three *vartulas* (circles) outside of that.

One should encircle the *thamavakta* with *lepāśākuśā*. On the second [layer], one should encircle it with the letters of the Mātṛkā in direct order (*anuloma*); on the third, one should encircle it with the letters of the Mātṛkā in reverse order (*pratiloma*). One should draw this in the form of a jar (*ghaṭa*), enclosed within a lotus. This "Jar-Bolt" (*Ghaṭārgala*) mantra, when accomplished through fire-offerings (*homa*) and other rites, fulfills the desires of the mind and accomplishes both seen and unseen goals. In this regard, worship grants all perfections (*siddhi*). Thus ends the *Pāśacī*.

*Takrom* is the *aṅkuśa* (goad) seed-syllable. *Āṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kroṃ* is the eight-syllabled mantra beginning with the *pāśa* (noose). *Hrīṃ gaurī rudradayite yogīśvarī huṃ phaṭ svāhā* is the sixteen-syllabled mantra beginning with *hṛllekhā*. These are the mantras according to the method of the Goddess in the *Sārasaṃgraha*: [the syllables] *aṣṭā*, *śā*, *pā*, *śā*, *ku*, *pra*, *k*, *pra*, *tya*, *ga*, *ar*, *ga*, *le*, *ha*, *la*, *ma*, *tha*, *pu*, *na*, *rā*, *g*, *ne*, *ya*, *mā*, *ru*, *te*, *ca*, *ha*, *ya*, *ma*, *da*, *kṣo*, *t*, *ta*, *re*, *ha*, *va*.

One should draw the syllables of *Ṛṇa*, *Nairṛta*, *Śaiva*, *Hara*, *Dvipa*, and *Tila* [in the petals]; and in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should draw the *Śakti* joined with the noose (*pāśa*), the goad (*aṅkuśa*), and the name of the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*). In the eight surrounding squares, which are beautified by the [remaining] letters, one should place the eight vowels. In the sixteen squares, the sixteen vowels and likewise the sixteen consonants; then the practitioner (*mantrī*) should place the *Māyā* (the syllable *Hrīm*) accompanied by the four vowels in the filaments of the lotus. On each of the petals, one should place the thirty consonants three times each, as well as the letters situated in the pericarp.

One should cause [the practitioner] to enter by means of the seed-syllables of the noose (pāśa) and the goad (aṅkuśa), and then cause him to enter the lotus by means of the syllables through the forward and reverse order of its petals: OṂ. Outside of that, one should draw the eight-petaled lotus situated within the jar, with two faces on each petal. The wise know that the seed-syllable of the noose (pāśabīja) is desired as being accompanied by the crescent of the moon, which is the night-maker (niśāśinaḥ) residing in the sky (khaṃ) and possessing the fire (dahana) of its own earth (nijabhūḥ). This is the auspicious noose (pāśaśrī).

Śakti, Smara, Manmatha, Śaktida, Daśāṅkuśa, Aṅkuśa—thus [one]; Kāminī, Rañjinī, Ṭha-dvaya—another; here, for the eight groups, Gaurī, Rudradayitā, Yogīśvarī, Sa-kavaca, Sna-ṭha-dvitaya. This sixteen-syllable Śākta mantra, beginning with the seed-syllables (*bīja*), has been declared. Its meaning: one should perform the recitation (*jāpa*) and other rites by enclosing the *śakti*-seed-syllable between the two *pāśa* syllables. Of this mantra, the *ghaṭārgala*...

The *laṃ-nāma* yantra will now be described. First, eight long lines called "bolts" (*argalā*), spreading out in the eight directions like the rays of the sun, should be drawn as pairs of intersecting lines. Then, having drawn a circle at the junction of the beginning of all those [lines], and again having drawn a circle above that, leaving a space of four finger-breadths, and again having drawn a circle in the middle of the region of all the bolts, one should [draw] lines outside of that as before.

Having drawn a circle with a measurement of one finger-breadth (*raṅgula*), one should again draw eight bars (*argalā*) starting from that circle within the intervals between the bricks (*iṣṭaka*) previously drawn;
these bars should be drawn equal in length to the previously drawn bars. One should also draw circular lines at the tips of those sixteen bars.
Furthermore, in the first circle, one should write the seed-syllables *āṃ hrīṃ krīṃ kroṃ ṣṭam*. Therein, [one should place] the goddess Bhuvaneśvarī by the side.

One should write the two syllables *Dvaṃdve* and *Pāśākuśau*, followed by the name of the practitioner (*sādhya*) and the name of Bhuvaneśvarī, starting from the middle [of the circle]. Then, outside the first circle, one should write the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of Bhuvaneśvarī in the eight corners. Again, similarly, on the third circle outside that, one should write the eight-syllable Śākta mantra in the eight directions: one should write the syllables *Āṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kroṃ*. Outside of that is the fourth circle...
In those eight squares, one should write the eight-syllable mantra of Śakti; again, outside of that, in sixteen squares, one should write the sixteen-syllable mantra;

and again, one should write the mantras of the eight *argalas* (bolts) according to the sequence to be described. Therein, in the first eastern *argala*, beginning from the north and ending with the *argala*, one should write the four syllables *oṃ paṃ lhaṃ lhāṃ lhiṃ lhīṃ* up to the pericarp (*karṇikā*), and then again in that same *argala*.

Starting from the *grāma* (the outer enclosure) on the right side, up to the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should write that seed-syllable *lhaṃ lhaṃ*; then, one should write the remaining two syllables. Again, starting from the right side of the western bar (*argalā*) up to the pericarp, one should write four of the six remaining seed-syllables—namely *lheṃ lholhauṃ lhauṃ lhaṃ lhaḥ*—up to the end of the bar; then, one should again write the remaining two seed-syllables starting from the front.

In the two *argalas* (bolts) of Agni and Vāyu in the east, one should write the forms of space (*viyat*) and wind (*vāyu*), namely the nature of the letter *ha*, as *hyaṃ hyāṃ* and so forth; thus, by dividing the four letters of Agni and the two of Vāyu, one should write them in pairs. Again, in the same manner, in the south and north, one should write the forms of space and wind joined with the letter *va*, as *vhaṃ vhāṃ* and so forth, totaling twelve. Again, in the same manner, in the *argalas* of Nirṛti and Īśāna, [one writes] space and fire...

One should write the twelve syllables beginning with *hraṃ*, *hrāṃ*, *ma*, and so forth, in the form of the letters *ja*, *ru*, *paṃ*, *kṛ*, *kā*, *ra*, *repha* (the letter *r*), and the vowels. This is the method for writing the *argalās*.

Furthermore, outside of all [this], having drawn an eight-petaled lotus joined at the junctions of the eight *argalās*, one should write upon each of its filaments—in the manner of *ām* and so forth—the fourth vowel together with the bindu (*m*), the two syllables of the *japa*, and the syllable *aṃsaḥ*. Then, again, within the centers of those petals, in a row...

One should write the syllables *kā*, *reṇa*, *yā*, *śa*, *kyam*, *kuśa*, and *bījāni* along with *āṃ kroṃ miḥ*; these three [groups] should be written everywhere. Having drawn two circles outside of that, one should encircle the first circle with the *pāśa* (noose) and the second with the *aṅkuśa* (goad). Having drawn two circles outside of that, one should encircle the first with the *mātṛkā* in direct order (*anuloma*) and the second with the *mātṛkā* in reverse order (*pratiloma*). By the word "and" (*ca*) in the phrase "with those moving in reverse order," the first... [is indicated].

It should be encircled by the *tuloga* [syllables]; outside of that, one should encircle it with the nine syllables known as the *kambha*. Outside of that, one should encircle it with the *repha* (the letter *r*) enclosed within the *ghaṭā* (the letter *gha*). By the word "also" (*api*), it is understood that one should encircle it with the *vakāra* (the letter *v*) prior to the encirclement by the *ghaṭā*. Having thus drawn the *ghaṭārgala* diagram, one should perform its worship. Now, first having performed the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭha*) and meditated, one should invoke [the deity].

Oṃ: One should worship the excellent enclosure with incense, flowers, and other offerings. In the four directions starting from the east—namely Hṛllekhā, Gaganā, Raktā, and Karālikā—this is the first enclosure. In the six corners, by means of the six long *māyā* seeds (*hrāṃ*, etc.), one worships the six limbs in the sequence beginning with "Hrāṃ to the heart"; this is the second [enclosure]. Then, in the third circle, starting from the east, one performs the third enclosure with the *mātṛkā* letters beginning with *a*.

With the *lokeśas* (the world-protectors) in the fourth and fourth [positions] and the fifth circle, thus are the five enclosures (*pañcāvaraṇāni*). Having worshipped these enclosures and again offered worship with perfumes and other offerings, one should thereafter install the bell according to the ritual procedure. Upon that, having installed the *caṇḍiyantṛa* (the fierce diagram) and worshipped it according to the ritual procedure, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) and so forth. As it is said, this becomes the bestower of success. Thus ends the procedure for drawing the *ghaṭārgala* diagram. [Thus ends Vimalā]
The ritual procedure for the *Saptaśatikā* contained within the *Tārābhaktitaraṅgiṇī* composed by Nanda is completed. May there be auspiciousness!
